biography: Pedro Aguiar, born in the bustling city of Belo Horizonte, Brazil, felt the call of speed early. Not from football pitches, but from the roaring engines echoing from a nearby karting track. His father, a mechanic with a passion for classic cars, recognized Pedro's inherent talent and scraped together enough to buy him a used kart. Pedro quickly dominated the local scene, his aggressive style and fearless overtaking maneuvers marking him as one to watch. His early career was marked by flashes of brilliance interspersed with costly errors, a trait that would follow him. A brief stint in Formula Inter MG-15 showed promise, but lacked consistent funding. He found a more stable home in Ginetta racing, bouncing between teams, never quite reaching the top step consistently. Now, at 37, the fire still burns, but the results are fading, leaving him a veteran with a reputation more for stubborn defense than outright speed.
drivingStyle: Pedro's driving style is a blend of raw aggression and calculated defense. He's known for late braking and squeezing every last bit of grip out of his tires, often at the expense of longevity. His defensive driving can be frustrating to opponents, as he will aggressively hold his line and make it incredibly difficult to pass. While quick in qualifying, his tire management often suffers in longer races, leading to late-race fade and missed opportunities. He tends to buckle under pressure, resorting to overly defensive tactics when challenged.

careerHighlight: Winning the Ginetta GT4 Supercup race at Curitiba in 2018 after a fierce battle with Ricardo Esteves. He held off Esteves's relentless attacks in the final laps to secure his biggest victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 2021 Ginetta Championship finale at Interlagos. The crash cost him a potential podium finish in the championship standings.
